description: Multi-phase plans currently in flight. Each phase references roadmap item ids; the activePhase section breaks the current phase into concrete tasks with status. Survives conversation compactions — a fresh session can pick up by reading this file.

phases.title: Foundation
phases.notes: Schema, bus, episodic memory, agent base. Nothing alive yet — just the substrate everything else hangs off.

phases.title: First Voice
phases.notes: Cheshire Cat end-to-end. Talking to himself. Layered context composer + engagement policy + ADR writer come online here because the Cat is their first consumer.

phases.title: First Tension
phases.notes: Add the White Rabbit. Two voices, role tension, semantic + relational memory layers populated as the agents accumulate history. Compaction-as-behavior arrives because it has to.

phases.title: First Race
phases.notes: Dodo orchestrator + quiescence + conflict resolution + first showcase (/health endpoint). The system runs end-to-end on a trivial directive. Init CLI lands here so the showcase can run against a real target project.

phases.title: Full Cast
phases.notes: Bring the rest of the cast online with integration tests per agent. Per-character artifact handlers for the new speech act payloads. Synthetic-consensus guard goes here because it only matters once disagreement is real.

phases.title: Real Threads
phases.notes: The hard showcases — translation chat MVP, security recovery, multi-session persistence. Transcript annotation tooling lets us publish them. Token telemetry confirms the engagement_policy is paying for itself.

phases.title: Evals
phases.notes: Generic-baseline vs Wonderland comparison. The compounding-curve plot is the legibility-of-value mitigation from §11. Without this the philosophy stays assertion.

activePhase.title: First Voice
activePhase.goal: The Cheshire Cat comes online — first character with a real voice. By end of P2, a Cat agent can receive a directive on the bus, deliberate using its constitution + episodic thread history, and produce a proposal Utterance with an ADR artifact attached. The Cat's silence stays valid: when no architectural decision is implicated, the Cat says nothing.
activePhase.sequencing: Composer first (gives compose_context something real to do — populate current_thread from episodic memory). Then engagement policy refinement (encode the Cat's structured rules from cheshire_cat.md III as data). Then ADR writer (the Cat needs somewhere to leave grins before it can deliberate). Finally the Cat itself: a WonderlandAgent subclass that ties everything together. The base class did its job; the Cat is the first proof that the substrate carries character.

tasks.title: Layered context composer — episodic thread history
tasks.details: Extend compose_context to populate Context.current_thread from EpisodicStore.query_by_thread, formatted as a chronological transcript. Constitution stays cached; thread snapshot goes in the uncached tail. Helper for formatting an utterance list as text.
tasks.resolution: WonderlandAgent.compose_context now async, queries EpisodicStore.query_by_thread for the trigger's thread, formats history as a transcript via new format_transcript helper, populates Context.current_thread. Triggers themselves are excluded from the history layer (they're presented separately as the immediate stimulus — duplicating them in the prompt would be wasteful). format_utterance + format_transcript exposed as public helpers (used by Context.to_llm_request and any agent that wants to render a transcript). speak() updated to await compose_context. Existing test that called compose_context synchronously updated. Six new tests cover: empty triggers → empty thread; population from memory; trigger exclusion; thread isolation; chronological order; helper behavior. 25 agent tests; 149 total pass; ruff clean.

tasks.title: Engagement policy: structured rules + LLM tiebreak
tasks.details: Build a structured EngagementRules dataclass that encodes per-speech-act engagement (always/selectively/rarely/almost-never) with optional predicate hooks per category (e.g., 'engage with ticket from Rabbit only when implementation hint constrains architecture'). Heuristic evaluation first; LLM tiebreak only when heuristic is uncertain (P2 lands the structure, LLM tiebreak deferred until we have a reason to need it).
tasks.resolution: src/wonderland/engagement.py — Engagement enum (always/selectively/rarely/almost_never), EngagementRule(speech_act, category, optional condition predicate), EngagementRules collection with first-match-wins ordering and a default tier. categorize() returns the matched tier (preserving the *why* for telemetry); should_engage() collapses to a binary engage/skip decision (engage iff tier ≠ ALMOST_NEVER). make_engagement_policy(rules) wraps rules into the EngagementPolicy callable Identity already accepts. Predicate helpers — speaker_is, addressed_to, body_contains_any, any_of, all_of — make rule construction read like the constitution prose. Tier-named factory functions (always, selectively, rarely, almost_never) keep call sites tight. LLM tiebreak deferred per the gameplan task — the structure makes adding it cheap when there's a real ambiguous case to resolve. 18 tests including a Cat-shaped rules sample that mirrors §III; 167 total pass; ruff clean.

tasks.title: ADR writer and registry
tasks.details: Service that takes an ADR artifact from a Cat proposal and writes it to <project_root>/.wonderland/architecture/adr-NNN-<slug>.md with auto-incrementing N. Validates Tradeoffs section is non-empty (the grin is non-optional). Registry queries: list_adrs, get_next_number, find_by_slug.

tasks.title: Cheshire Cat agent — first end-to-end
tasks.details: Concrete WonderlandAgent subclass for the Cat. Loads constitutions/cheshire_cat.md. Engagement policy from T9 wired with the Cat's specific rules. compose_context overrides T8 if needed. deliberate calls LLMClient.complete and parses the response into a Utterance (proposal/question/reframe/concern/deference) with optional ADR artifact. End-to-end test: directive → Cat produces proposal → ADR file appears at .wonderland/architecture/adr-001-*.md. Live test gated behind WONDERLAND_LLM_SMOKE.
